title: Lambda inside a VPC, and the cost that used to carry

videos.script: Your function needs a database, and the database has no public address. So the function goes into your VPC. {{why}} That decision has a price on each side, and this lesson names both. First, what a VPC gives a function, and what it does not. It gives an address next to the database. It gives no protection, because nothing could reach the function anyway. {{config}} You will configure one against moto, and watch moto accept a subnet that does not exist. {{enis}} Then the history. Until 2019, every new environment waited seconds for a network interface of its own. That is why people still say to keep Lambda out of VPCs. Today the interface is shared, and made in advance. {{out}} What remains is the way out. A function in a private subnet loses the internet, even the public endpoints of AWS. A NAT gateway brings it back, by the hour and by the gigabyte. An endpoint brings back one service, and for S3 it is free. You will price both from the sheet.
